comment: No source is published and the maker's site carries no manual for it. Traffic, Water and Hotel are one piece of hardware with three overlays, and the VCV plugin builds them as three models sharing a panel layout: three jacks across the top, a three-by-three knob grid, a three-way Mode switch, a two-way Voltage Range switch, three CV outputs and a pulse output. The knobs are all configured 0 to 1 with a default of 0, and the scaling is the same in all three models: value times 8 on the Unipolar setting, value times 16 minus 8 on Bipolar, so the CV outputs span 0 to 8V or -8V to +8V rather than the usual 10. Traffic's three trigger inputs are the only ones in the plugin that test against 0.3V; Water's and Hotel's test against 1V. The Mode switch's three choices are configured as Groove, ?? and Base at values 0, 1 and 2; the panel prints Base at the top of the toggle, ?? at the middle and Groove at the bottom, which matches a toggle whose lowest position is value 0. In the ?? mode the module fills three sixteen-entry tables with three-bit random numbers and reads the knobs through them; the exact stepping of those tables was not followed far enough to describe on a control's own line.
